legal_filer_name_note: IRS filings and the DuckDB organizations spine carry this EIN under its legal filer name, Tri-angel Unlimited (care of Texas Empowerment Academy). The school's own site and all public-facing materials use Texas Empowerment Academy; that is the name used throughout this page.
mission: We Are a Pre-K through 12 charter school, cultural hub, and community center serving Austin-area families. We Provide our students with a sound education in a nurturing environment conducive to academic excellence that promotes a sense of community and self-responsibility.
programs: Cultural hub and community center serving Austin-area families
Empowerment system providing access to self-help opportunities for social, emotional, spiritual, and economic growth
Student support addressing social, mental, emotional, and academic needs together, not academics alone
focus_areas: Character and leadership development (core values: Education, Character, Leadership)
Community empowerment through service, learning, and volunteerism (the three Cs of African existence: communalism, collectivism, cooperation)
ntee_code_note: BMF-filed code (S20/Community Improvement) does not read as a typical school filing code (most Pre-K-12 schools file under B/Education); Texas Empowerment Academy's own site frames itself explicitly as school AND cultural hub AND community center together, which likely explains the S-code filing. Funder peer-matching below is run against this filed code, not a re-assigned B-code, per this Drive's rule that filed codes are used as filed.
target_populations: Pre-K through 12th grade students in East Austin
Primarily African-American students and families (per third-party school-profile aggregators; not independently verified against the school's own enrollment data)
Families seeking culturally relevant, community-centered education

reported_scale.note: 2023 Form 990 (most recent processed return, ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer API, EIN 742782958): total revenue $5,041,668; total expenses $6,597,148; total assets (EOY) $29,147,401. Third-party aggregators (GreatSchools, U.S. News) separately report approximately 413 students in grades 3-12 with a 17:1 student-teacher ratio; not independently re-verified against the school's own enrollment records and shown here as reported, not confirmed.
